session.join_model: private invite lobby plus shared-authority public FIFO matchmaking; empty seats filled by random-ID bots after an 8-second wait; no bot identity label per explicit user request
session.late_join: Reject mid-match joins; original members resume within 30 seconds

topology.authority_owner: PC Node server; same rules in phone host worker
trust_assumptions: Trusted LAN friends; phone host can inspect its own authority runtime
No production identity or cloud currency service exists
topology.host_migration: None: host loss cancels unfinished game
risk_acceptance: Phone host owns private state; local save balances are editable. Public Internet service is not deployed; configured shared endpoint supports matchmaking, and public ranked play remains disabled.

authority_validation: 2 to 4 connected ready members; host alone starts private matches
Matchmaker alone forms four-seat automatic matches, removing canceled or disconnected peers
Bots choose using their own hand plus public information; no hidden opponent cards or cursed positions are passed to bot policy
Own hand only; 1 to 3 distinct cards

Immutable immediately previous claim records actor, round, table target and manual/timeout source; target ordinary cards and thief wildcard are truthful; only accused for a lie or caller for all-truth is punished
Authority shuffles one cursed position among six
Loser alone drinks; last survivor wins
Local camp credits winner 30 once; losers 0

simulation.clock: Discrete authority revisions with serverTime, phaseAt and fixed roundAt; 6s reveal, 8s potion preparation, 4.8s outcome including 1.8s sipping; reconnect pause shifts presentation clock and preserves remaining deadline. Mobile portrait prompt does not pause or reset multiplayer timers.
simulation.tick_rate_basis: This game resolves discrete commands and does not require a continuous simulation tick.
simulation.prediction: Client may preview legal targets but never applies an outcome as final.
simulation.reconciliation: Every accepted action broadcasts an authorized snapshot; stale revision rejects requests.
simulation.measurement_plan: Capture join, active-turn, reveal, drink, reconnect and completion in Node and native LAN harness tests.

replication.model: reliable commands plus canonical state snapshots
replication.interest_management: All public match state reaches members; private hand state reaches only its owner.
replication.hidden_state: Only own hand reaches a member. Per-round plays expose owner/count/table/time/source only, allowing per-seat piles to survive reconnect. Only the challenged newest batch reveals card kinds via the event. Older piles remain face-down. Cursed bottle positions never appear in snapshots.

transport.primary: WebSocket on trusted LAN; WSS endpoint configuration for future public service; local worker fallback for unconfigured Android matching
transport.rationale: Reliable ordered commands fit the card game and existing Android LAN socket bridge.
transport.fallback: Without serverUrl browsers use same-origin authority and Android uses local bot table. Public DNS, TLS and server deployment are not provisioned.
transport.backpressure: PC sockets close when outbound queue exceeds 128 KiB; incoming frames capped at 16 KiB; 30 requests per second per member.

lifecycle.reconnect: Opaque random resume token bound to client id and seat; 30 second grace, fresh own-hand snapshot.
lifecycle.disconnect: Pause a live unfinished match; cancel without rewards when a player leaves or grace expires. Phone host background stops native room. 30-second turn timer pauses during reconnect; on expiry the authority plays one random owned card.
lifecycle.version_policy: Reject messages other than protocol v1; validate websocket v1 endpoint.

security.identity: Random per-tab client id and random per-seat resume token, no cloud account.
security.authorization: Validate room, member, host, phase, hand ownership, action id and revision.
validation: validate every message against the protocol schema
reject duplicate or stale action identifiers
calculate movement, combat, inventory, and rewards on the server
security.logging: Client-visible public event history; never log resume tokens, cursed positions or hidden hands.

metrics: Test join count and completion rounds
Queue wait and actual human/bot counts; solo-vs-bot outcome history separate from mixed-human matches
traces: Current revision and public event history
alerts: Visible connection status and malformed/stale command error; no operational cloud alerting

scenarios: Private snapshot capture for four clients
Forced last-hand challenge and wildcard truth
One queued human receives three bots; four queued humans receive none
Queue cancellation, disconnect cleanup, duplicate queue request and no public join into private rooms
Bot actions remain legal and private-information isolation is maintained
acceptance: Private cards never leak through the public snapshot
Rejected commands do not mutate canonical revision
Winner 30 and loser 0 recorded once per match

decisions.decision: Share deterministic pure rules between PC authority and phone worker
decisions.reason: Same rules and bot behavior on LAN authority and local worker; future serverUrl routes matching to shared independent authority
decisions.evidence: games/liars/rules.js and rooms.js used by both server.mjs and phone-worker.js
